transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

I have noted the 22E code on your Samsung display; while this is a controller report and not proof of a failed part, this step is the right place to start. Let’s narrow it down. Please keep the doors shut as much as you can. A fridge should be at 5°C or below: chilled food that has been warmer than 8°C for more than about four hours is safest thrown away, and food that has fully thawed shouldn't be refrozen unless it's cooked first. Is it just the fridge that's warm, just the freezer, or both?
Just the fridge side is warm, it's reading 9C. The freezer side is fine. No burning smell or tripping of the electrics either.

A fridge freezer can take up to a day to recover if a door was left ajar or if a large amount of warm food was placed inside. This is normal behaviour for the appliance to reach its set temperature again. Please allow some time for this process to complete before assuming there is a fault. Has a door been left open or not shut properly recently, or has a lot of warm food gone in?
Not that I know of, no door left open. The code first appeared 2 days ago and the fridge is still at 9C, so it doesn't seem to be recovering.

Thanks for letting us know about the doors being shut. Please check the temperature dial or display to ensure the fridge is around 3–5°C and the freezer at -18°C, and confirm that no holiday or eco mode is active. You might find the attached image helpful for reference. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
I haven't changed any settings or put it in a holiday/eco mode as far as I know. The fridge temperature is just reading 9C. What should I check next?

Sorry, I didn't quite catch which of these it is. Please check the temperature dial or display to ensure the fridge is about 3–5°C and the freezer -18°C. Also, make sure no holiday or eco mode is currently active. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
Everything's set normally, no mode left on and nothing corrected. It's just reading 9C. Airflow from the fridge vents is very weak too, if that helps. What should I check next?

Thanks for confirming the settings are normal. I’ve noted the 9C code on the display; this next step is the right place to start regardless. Cold air enters through vents, usually located on the back wall inside the fridge section. Please ensure no food items are pressed directly against these vents and that the shelves are not packed so tightly that airflow is restricted. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
I'm not sure, I don't think anything is blocking the vents but I haven't looked closely. The airflow is still very weak though. Is there anything else I should check?

Thanks for letting me know it is still warm. I didn't quite catch which of these it is. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?

Nothing is pressed against the vents as far as I can tell, and the shelves aren't packed tight. Airflow is still very weak. Is this something that needs an engineer, or is there anything else I can check myself?

Thanks for letting us know the vents are clear and it’s still warm. Please run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door to check for splits, gaps, or sections that have come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Just look and feel along the rubber — don't pull or cut it. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
The door seals look fine on both doors, no splits or gaps and they close flat. Still 9C with weak airflow though. Anything else I can check?

Thanks for confirming the door seal and temperature status. On most frost-free models, a fan pushes cold air from the freezer into the fridge. To check if it’s working, open the freezer and press in the little door switch (or light button). You should hear a fan whirr at the back. Please just listen from the outside — don't take any covers off or touch anything at the back. Can you hear the fan running when you do that, or is it silent?
